title: Approved Architecture Review
body:
Overview

This record documents Approved Architecture Review within the Secure Communications Assurance Database. Evaluates approved communications architectures, reliability and configuration compliance. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record checks an approved communications design against its own configuration standard: each required setting is listed, each is checked, and the compliance result is the counted fraction that passes. Reliability is modeled from link history, and backup paths are verified by test, not assumed.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: PASS - approved settings applied. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A communications engineer uses these records to prove a configuration is compliant, to find the settings that drifted, and to confirm that a backup path works before it is needed. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Approved Architecture Review: score configuration compliance from counted checks.
checks = [('approved settings applied', True), ('backup path tested', True), ('access list reviewed', True), ('rotation schedule current', True), ('monitoring coverage complete', True), ('change log signed', False)]
passed = sum(1 for _, ok in checks if ok)
for name, ok in checks:
    print(("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"), "-", name)
print("checks:", len(checks), "passed:", passed)
print("compliance fraction:", round(passed / len(checks), 3))
demo_output:
PASS - approved settings applied
PASS - backup path tested
PASS - access list reviewed
PASS - rotation schedule current
PASS - monitoring coverage complete
FAIL - change log signed
checks: 6 passed: 5
compliance fraction: 0.833
